Underwater lanterns glow amber beneath the surface, lighting the steam from inside so it rises gold at the base and fades into deep blue overhead, every wet rim stone catching the warm upward cast.
A stone lantern's flame throws orange across the nearest drift of steam, which rolls thick over the rim and spreads downhill across the wet stone, the far side of the pool swallowed in teal shadow.
Five round paper lanterns hang above the water, each a soft amber blur inside the rising steam, the steam climbing slow coils between them until it thins into a violet sky already pricked with stars.
The inn's windows behind push rose-gold light across the water and into the rolling bank of steam, which stands low and full above the surface, the far rim only half reading through the haze.
A huge low moon clears the ridge and turns the thick steam silver in front of it, the water beneath almost black, the nearest stones catching cold white light against the deep blue of the sky above.

The last band of sunset burns orange low behind whatever closes the far distance under a sky already deep blue, the steam catching that low warmth at the bottom of each slow coil, cooling to grey-violet before it thins overhead.

A brazier beside the pool throws orange upward into the drifting steam, which is pushed flat and sideways by the heat rising from the coals, every wet edge nearest the fire flashing amber against the dark teal water.

A scatter of small warm bulbs on a wire along the fence glows through the steam in nine soft dots, three set slightly apart from the rest, the steam pressing close around each bulb and turning it a deep gold against slate-blue air.

One candle burns in a stone niche at the rim, its glow landing low on the nearest bank of steam, which rolls over that edge and runs downhill across the stone in slow amber rolls, the rest of the pool in cool blue-grey.
A lit walkway lamp on a post fills its cone with moving steam, the steam climbing through warm gold light and carrying it upward before losing it to a violet night sky above.

Starlight and the cold pale glow off nearby surfaces together light the steam a grey-blue as it stands in a low bank over almost-black water, the only warmth a faint amber bleed from somewhere far behind.

A small carried lantern set down on a rim stone throws its light low and close, turning the nearest thick curl of steam deep gold while the steam veiling the far rim holds nothing but cool blue darkness.

A scatter of tiny warm lights far off in the distance lights the near face of the rolling steam orange while the far side of each curl stays in cold blue-grey, the water between reflecting both in broken patches.

Underwater lanterns push amber up through the surface so the steam is lit from beneath, its base burning gold and its slow climb fading into deep violet overhead, the far rim only a pale suggestion through the veil.
A stone lantern flame casts its orange glow across a thick drift of steam that stands in a low bank over the water, the warm orange giving way to cool teal shadow at the pool's far edge.

Seven paper lanterns hang in a loose line, two of them drifted apart from the others, their warm yellow glow diffused by the rising steam until each is a soft blurred core of gold in the blue-grey air.

The windows behind the pool push warm amber light across the water's surface and into the base of the steam, which rolls thick over the nearest rim and runs down the wet stone while the upper drift stays cool blue.

The low moon sits enormous behind a slow climb of steam, turning it silver and pale against a deep blue sky, the water below holding a long cold path of moonlight broken only where the steam veil thickens.
Sunset's last orange band behind the ridgeline lights the bottom of the steam from below, each slow coil catching that warmth before it rises into blue and then into the first stars of the evening.

A brazier beside the rim throws orange up into thick drifting steam that has been pushed flat and sideways by the heat, the warm orange face of each drift contrasting sharply with the cool teal face turned away from the fire.

Underwater lanterns glow warm through the dark water, their amber light catching every rising curl of steam close to the surface, the steam carrying that gold upward until it dissolves into a cool grey-blue sky.

A small carried lantern on the rim stone angles its glow into the bank of steam rolling over the edge, the steam lit amber and gold nearest the flame and shading into a deep slate-blue as it spreads across the cool water.
A lit post lamp stands at the edge, its warm cone full of slow-moving steam that climbs through the gold light and carries a faint amber into the violet air above before thinning to nothing.

Tiny warm bulbs on a wire above the pool — eleven in total, one set distinctly apart — glow through the rising steam, each one a soft gold core ringed in deep blue-grey where the steam thickens between them.

One candle in a rim niche throws its small orange glow into the nearest heavy curl of steam, which climbs past it and veils the far side of the pool completely, leaving only a pale teal suggestion of the far rim in the dark.
